Verdict: ACCEPTThe two-source obstruction and the source-separated gate lemma are correct in the stated abstract capacity model. The four reported totals—225, 211, 14, and 120—also agree with a direct combinatorial count of the checker’s actual search space. I find no blocking mathematical gap.There is one scope wording correction to make: “every nonempty two-source network with two gates and two resources” is broader than what the checker enumerates. The precise family is given below. There is also a vacuous assertion to remove or repair, although the substantive source-separated checks occur elsewhere in the loop and are valid.This is a review by mathematical reasoning and inspection of the supplied code and output. I did not execute the checker. No Lean source or proof was included, so this verdict does not certify any Lean formalization or kernel check.1. The one-mixed-gate obstruction is correctWrite  $\mu(G)$  for the maximum matching size in the source-resource reachability projection, and  $\nu(G)$  for the maximum legal route packing.Every legal packing projects to a matching: its sources are distinct, its terminal resources are distinct, and each selected pair is connected by a route. Consequently,
$$\nu(G)\leq \mu(G).$$
The reverse inequality need not hold because a projected edge records the existence of an individual route without recording the internal capacities that route consumes.In the displayed example:Both sources reach both resources, so the projection is  $K_{2,2}$  and  $\mu(G)=2$ .Every source-resource route passes through  $g$ .The capacity-one split arc for  $g$  therefore bounds every legal route packing by one.At least one route exists, so this upper bound is attained.Thus
$$\mu(G)=2,\qquad \nu(G)=1,$$
and the deficit is exactly one. The displayed  $A(G)=2$  is consistent with the note’s quota notation.The distinction concerning resource identity is also correct. Assigning  $R_0$  to  $A$  and  $R_1$  to  $B$  respects resource capacities. The failure is that both assignments require the same capacity-one mixed gate.More precisely, the projection checks simultaneous allocation of distinct endpoints, with each assigned pair justified individually by reachability. It does not check whether the witnessing routes can coexist. This is exactly why a quota bound obtained from that projection cannot automatically supply the route-flow bound.The example is minimal in the intended gate-capacity model: a strict gap requires projection matching size at least two, hence at least two sources and two resources; the stated obstruction then uses just one mixed gate.2. The source-separated gate lemma is validThe proof establishes its conclusion directly.Let  $M$  be the matching, and for every matched source  $s$ , choose a directed path  $P_s$  to its assigned resource  $r_s$ . If reachability was witnessed by a walk, cycles can first be deleted.Suppose two paths  $P_s$  and  $P_t$ , with  $s\ne t$ , used the same mixed gate  $g$ . Their respective initial segments would show that
$$s\leadsto g
\quad\text{and}\quad
t\leadsto g.$$
This contradicts the hypothesis that at most one alpha source reaches  $g$ .Hence the paths are pairwise gate-disjoint. Their resource endpoints are distinct because they come from a matching, and each source is used once. This proves the lemma.The argument also justifies equality in the nonsaturating casesThe proof does not require the matching to saturate every source in the network. It works for any matching by choosing paths only for its matched sources. Therefore source separation implies
$$\boxed{\nu(G)=\mu(G).}$$
This matters for the enumeration: some of the 120 source-separated cases have unmatched or unreachable sources. Their equality assertion is still justified; the note is not restricted to cases with a perfect source-resource matching.The capacity model should remain explicitThe sentence “a legal unit-capacity route packing” uses the intended convention that source quotas, terminal resource capacities, and mixed-gate capacities are the relevant constraints. In particular, sources and resources serve as terminals, and any additional shared object whose capacity must be enforced must be represented in the capacity model.Gate-disjointness would not, by itself, enforce an additional capacity-one object that had been omitted from that model. This is a clarification of the abstract model, not a counterexample to the lemma as intended.“Local” needs a precise readingThe hypothesis is checked separately for each gate, but it concerns source reachability, which may require tracing upstream routes. It is not merely a condition on immediate source-to-gate edges.For example, in
$$A\to g_0\to g_1,\qquad B\to g_1,$$
each gate has at most one immediate incoming edge from a source, yet  $g_1$  is reachable from both sources. The lemma correctly excludes this situation because it uses reachability.The checker’s direct-incidence test is correct for its three-layer networks, where gates cannot be reached through other gates. For the general lemma, I would replace “local, checkable” with:“checkable gate by gate from the source-reachability sets.”The assertion that source separation is stronger than necessary is also correct. For instance, if both sources connect to both gates and both gates connect to both resources, source separation fails, but two gate-disjoint routes exist.3. The enumeration counts are correct, but its scope needs precise wordingThe actual enumerated family consists of labeled simple directed networks
$$\{A,B\}\longrightarrow\{g_0,g_1\}
\longrightarrow\{R_0,R_1\},$$
with edges only between consecutive layers and with both edge layers nonempty.The checker does not enumerate arbitrary directed networks on these six vertices. It includes no gate-to-gate edges, direct source-resource edges, or other edge types.A precise replacement for the opening of §3 is:The verifier enumerates all 225 labeled simple three-layer networks on two sources, two gates, and two resources, with edges only from sources to gates and from gates to resources, and with each of the two edge layers nonempty.This qualification is necessary even within the layered model. If “nonempty” meant merely “at least one edge anywhere,” there would be
$$2^8-1=255$$
networks. The checker omits the 30 networks with exactly one empty layer. Every omitted case has both projection matching size and route flow zero, so their omission does not conceal another obstruction.Here is a direct derivation of all four reported totals.QuantityDerivationTotalEnumerated networks $(2^4-1)^2$  $225$ Source-separated networks $(3^2-1)(2^4-1)$  $120$ Strict projection overstatements $8+8-2$  $14$ Exact projections $225-14$  $211$ Total networks: 225Each layer has four possible edges. Each mask ranges over its 15 nonzero possibilities. Thus
$$15\cdot15=225.$$
Source-separated networks: 120For each gate, its incoming-source set must be one of
$$\varnothing,\quad \{A\},\quad \{B\}.$$
There are  $3^2$  choices for the two gates. Removing the choice with no source-gate edges leaves eight possibilities. The outgoing layer may be any of its 15 nonempty configurations, giving
$$(3^2-1)\cdot15=120.$$
The most precise wording is that the condition holds in 120 cases, and equality is asserted in every such case. The condition itself is evaluated in all 225 cases.Strict overstatements: 14A strict gap must have
$$\mu(G)=2,\qquad \nu(G)=1.$$
Indeed, projection size zero forces route flow zero, and projection size one guarantees at least one route.In this two-by-two-by-two layered model, a packing of size two exists exactly when both individual layers have perfect matchings:Two disjoint routes provide such matchings.Conversely, a source-gate perfect matching and a gate-resource perfect matching compose through the two gates into two legal routes.Under  $\mu(G)=2$ , failure therefore takes one of two forms.First family: both sources are confined to one gate.Both sources connect only to a gate  $g$ , and  $g$  connects to both resources. The other gate can connect to any subset of resources. This gives
$$2\cdot4=8$$
networks.Second family: all resource access is confined to one gate.One gate  $g$  connects to both resources, the other gate has no outgoing edges, and both sources connect to  $g$ . Each source may independently also connect to the other gate. This gives another
$$2\cdot4=8$$
networks.The intersection consists of the two choices of a sole active gate. Hence the number of strict gaps is
$$8+8-2=14.$$
The remaining
$$225-14=211$$
networks have exact projection.These are mathematical counts of the stated finite family, not an inference from the reported PASS.4. Checker inspection and evidentiary limitsThe substantive algorithms match this finite modelroute_flow recursively considers, for each source, either using no route or selecting a source-gate-resource route. It tracks used gates and resources, so it exhausts exactly the legal packings in the layered model.bipartite_matching uses an augmenting-path search to calculate the matching size of the reachability projection.The source-separation branch contains a real assertion:Pythonassert quota == flowThat is the operative equality check for the 120 qualifying cases.The final conditional assertion is vacuousThis line does not perform the apparent count comparison:Pythonassert totals['source_separated_controls'] == totals['source_separated_exact'] if 'source_separated_exact' in totals else TrueThe key source_separated_exact is never created. The conditional therefore selects True.This line should be removed or replaced with an actual check. It does not invalidate the source-separated controls, because the equality assertion inside the loop is already substantive.The script also reports, rather than explicitly asserts, the four exact numerical totals. The supplied output is consistent with the code and with the independent count above; inspecting that consistency is different from certifying the recorded execution.5. The limits of the result are appropriately statedThe multiplicity- $m$  sentence is acceptable as a pointer to a separate low-congestion result. It should retain the distinction between bounded congestion and full compensation. For example,  $k$  supplied paths with distinct source and resource endpoints and gate congestion at most  $m$  give a feasible fractional flow of value  $k/m$ . In the usual finite integral-capacity route network, this yields an integral packing of size at least
$$\left\lceil \frac{k}{m}\right\rceil.$$
It does not generally yield all  $k$  routes or preserve every prescribed source-resource pairing. The note does not claim those stronger conclusions.The physical scope is also correctly limited. The note establishes an obstruction to replacing internal-capacity routing by endpoint reachability matching, together with a sufficient condition making that replacement valid. It neither constructs a physical-grid realization nor derives a universal route-cover or  $5/6$  theorem.The accepted result is therefore the abstract bridge statement. The required editorial cleanup is to specify the enumeration family exactly; the vacuous assertion is a nonblocking checker cleanup.
